newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends higher, but resistance intact.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends higher, but resistance intact.

text.p: Speculative short covering bolstered CSCE cocoa futures on Thursday, but steady scale-up selling by the trade and currency-related arbitrage sales kept prices from breaching key resistance levels, dealers said.
Spot March futures rose $12 a tonne on the day, to $1,320, after ranging between $1,325 and $1,306. Most-active May ended up $13, to $1,347, while the rest gained $10 to $11.
The day's volume was moderate, at an estimated 6,399 lots.
Traders said a report by E.D.& F. Man lent support to the market, but was not bullish enough to spark a strong rally or push the March through resistance at the day's high of $1,325.
Man saw a global production deficit of between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes in 1996/97 due to strong consumption and an estimated decline in output.
Man put the Ivorian harvest at 1.050 million tonnes, down from its last estimate for 1995/96 of 1.1 million given a slower arrivals data.

But crops in Brazil were likely to suffer and growth in Indonesia was slowing, resulting in a drop of 10 percent in world production to 2.586 million tonnes. Consumption was expected to increase by 2.5-3 percent.
Traders much the activity continued to focus on the nearby switch, as operators rolled spot March into second-month May ahead of March's delivery period February 14.
Technically, traders pegged March reisitance at $1,325-$1,330, while support was seen at $1,300-$1,295, then $1,280.
